header:
Date: 2026-04-08 | Time: 10:00 AM PDT | Duration: 58 mins
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood Solutions), Priya (Redwood CSM), Dr. Mira Kapoor (Helix Head of ML), Tom Ng (CTO), Aisha (Data Eng), Jon Ruiz (Security), Sana (PM)
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood Inference for Helix’s clinical note summarization pipeline. Agreed success criteria (latency, throughput, quality thresholds), access path (VPC peering or temporary S3 + service account), benchmark plan (5k queries, warmup + steady-state), mid-point review and exec readout dates. Action items and owners captured.
topics: POC timeline & milestones (kickoff, access, mid-point, exec readout)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (AE): Good morning everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick intros then we can jump into the milestone checklist for the POC - we scoped ~6 weeks in the deck but want to lock dates.
[00:18] Dr. Mira Kapoor (Helix): Hi, Mira here. We are excited; main ask is to prove latency down to a p95 under 450ms for our summarization workload and keep hallucination rate <3% on clinical notes.
[00:35] Lena (SE): Great, thanks Mira. To be clear, are those constraints for the hosted API or private deployment? There are different tradeoffs.
[00:45] Tom Ng (CTO): For the pilot we prefer Redwood hosted with private data path - e.g., S3 presigned upload + redwood-team will not persist PII. If that looks promising we may move to a dedicated VPC test.
[01:05] Samir: OK that's useful. For the kickoff milestones I propose: this week - access & SOW; week 2 - access verified + warmup; week 3-4 - steady-state benchmarks; week 5 - mid-point readout; week 6 - exec readout. Is that alignment?
[01:25] Sana (PM): That timeline maps to internal calendars but we need a hard mid-point demo week of 2026-05-12.
[01:36] Lena: Noted. On benchmarks, we'll run a two-phase run: warmup (2 hours load) to populate KV cache and prefixes, then steady-state 4 hours at target QPS. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, error rate, and per-response score vs your reference summaries.
[02:00] Aisha (Data Eng): For the dataset, we can produce an anonymized 5k-query set covering short/long notes. Average request is ~450 tokens input, expected output ~120 tokens.
[02:16] Diego (Solutions Eng): That helps sizing. With those numbers our rough token volume for a 4-hour steady-state at 5 qps is ~5qps * 3600 * 4 * (450+120) tokens = big number, we'll include precise calc in the spreadsheet.
[02:36] Jon (Security): From security: SOC2 is table stakes; we also need KMS for keys, customer-managed keys preferred for dedicated. For hosted pilot we need attestations that data is ephemeral and we can prove no long-term storage of PII.
[02:56] Lena: We can share our SOC2 report and a security FAQ. For the pilot we support scoped retention and audit logs; KMS integration is supported on Dedicated and via customer-managed key on Private installs.
[03:12] Samir: Success criteria recap — agreed items: 1) p95 latency <=450ms on target model under steady-state; 2) 99th percentile error rate <0.5%; 3) output quality: ROUGE-L / human eval pass rate >= 92% vs your gold; 4) cost target <= $X per 1k tokens (we'll fill number in pricing SOW). Any other must-haves?
[03:36] Dr. Mira Kapoor: Also need reproducible eval scripts; we want to run the same scoring locally against a held-out set.
[03:44] Lena: We'll provide the evaluation harness and the scoring script; we'll version it in the benchmark spreadsheet so it's deterministic.
[03:52] Sana: For stakeholders, exec readout needs Tom + Mira + Head of Clinical Ops to attend; can Redwood provide a one-pager with top-line metrics and recommended next steps?
[04:05] Samir: Yes, we'll produce an exec readout slide deck and a short one-pager. We'll schedule the readout for week of 2026-05-18 unless you prefer earlier.
[04:18] Tom Ng: Week of 5/18 is fine. Can we also include a comparison vs Anthropic/OG API so execs can see vendor tradeoffs?
[04:29] Samir: We can include competitor comparison for throughput/latency/cost but won't include proprietary benchmarks we don't run. We'll add public reference numbers and note that direct apples-to-apples comparisons are in the benchmark spreadsheet if you want us to run them.
[04:45] Aisha: On access: we prefer to provide an S3 location with anonymized data and a service account for Redwood to pull. We need a short runbook for credentials and optional VPC peering.
[04:58] Diego: Action: I'll create a runbook with both S3 presigned and VPC peering steps; for the latter we'll need a point-of-contact for network setup.
[05:08] Jon: I'll be that contact. Also, audit logs must be exportable to our SIEM. Is that supported?
[05:16] Lena: Yes, we can stream audit logs to your AWS account for the pilot; we'll document retention settings.
[05:22] Samir: Pricing: the pilot pricing in SOW will include a flat monthly access credit plus overage token rates; I'll send the draft. If you want dedicated capacity estimate we'll include an optional appendix.
[05:36] Dr. Mira Kapoor: Operationally, what's your recommended canary during the mid-point? We want a rollback plan in case quality regressions appear.
[05:46] Diego: We'll run an A/B canary with traffic split 10/90 to the new model variant and watch quality signals from the eval harness. The rollback is automatic if error thresholds exceed configured limits. We'll share the rollout policy in the runbook.
[06:01] Sana: For mid-point readout, we want to see steady-state metrics, examples of failures, and proposed remediation.
[06:09] Lena: Yep, we'll include example failed summaries and suggested prompt/template changes or model variant recommendations.
[06:17] Tom: For the internal team, what level of telemetry do we get? Token-level cost breakdowns and per-model lat/throughput?
[06:25] Priya (CSM): Full telemetry is available in the Redwood Console for the pilot; we'll enable dashboard access for Helix stakeholders.
[06:33] Jon: Any contractual constraints about data retention in logs? We need to ensure no PHI persists.
[06:40] Samir: We'll add a clause in the SOW about ephemeral retention for pilot data, and we can agree to a short retention window for logs and purge after the pilot unless Helix requests export.
[06:51] Dr. Mira Kapoor: Sounds good. Minor point: can the eval harness compute medical-entity-aware hallucination metrics or do you rely on broad ROUGE/human score?
[07:02] Lena: We can extend the scoring script to include entity-level precision/recall for a small label set you provide. That will be part of the benchmark spreadsheet checklist.
[07:12] Sana: Okay, next steps recap?
[07:15] Samir: I'll send SOW + pricing by Friday 4/10. Lena will upload benchmark plan + scripts by 4/9. Helix provides anonymized dataset and network contact by 4/12. Diego to prepare runbook by 4/11. Mid-point review week of 5/11 and exec readout week of 5/18.
[07:38] Tom: All sounds good. One last question — if we hit the success criteria early, what's a typical ramp path to Dedicated?
[07:47] Samir: We do a post-pilot sizing review, provide Dedicated capacity estimate with SLA options, and can lock a reserved commit within 2–3 weeks after exec approval.
[07:57] Dr. Mira Kapoor: Great, thanks everyone.
[08:00] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and invite for the mid-point.
[08:05] (call ends)
